What are you waiting for?</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"201341983":0,"335551550":1,"335551620":1,"335559685":0,"335559737":0,"335559738":240,"335559739":240,"335559740":279}"> </span></p></div><h4>Role: Senior Trading Manager</h4> <p><strong>Brand: Myprotein</strong></p> <p><strong>Reporting to: Ecommerce Director </strong></p> <p><strong>Location: THG ICON 1, 7-9 Sunbank Lane, WA15 0AF (Fully Office Based) </strong></p> <p data-pm-slice="1 3 []">As Senior Trading Manager for the UK, you will own the commercial performance of Myprotein's UK website, driving profitable growth through effective ecommerce trading, customer experience and onsite optimisation.</p> <p>You will set the UK ecommerce strategy, translating commercial objectives and customer insight into clear trading priorities. Combining strong commercial judgement with data-led decision-making, you will identify opportunities, drive performance and lead cross-functional teams to deliver growth.</p> <h2>The Details</h2> <ul> <li>Own UK website performance across revenue, traffic, conversion, AOV, margin and profitability.</li> <li>Set and deliver the UK ecommerce trading strategy, translating business targets into clear priorities and action plans.</li> <li>Drive onsite trading and optimisation across merchandising, navigation, search, landing pages and promotional activity.</li> <li>Manage pricing and promotional investment, balancing revenue growth, margin and customer experience.</li> <li>Lead forecasting and performance reviews, identifying risks, opportunities and actions to maximise trading performance.</li> <li>Use customer insight, competitor activity and market trends to inform commercial decisions and identify growth opportunities.</li> <li>Partner with Marketing, CRM, Brand, Product, UX, Technology, Supply Chain and Finance to deliver the UK growth agenda.</li> <li>Drive improvements across the customer journey, increasing conversion, basket size, retention and customer lifetime value.</li> <li>Lead testing and optimisation initiatives, using clear hypotheses and measurable commercial outcomes.</li> <li>Champion AI, automation and analytics to improve decision-making, efficiency and trading effectiveness.</li> <li>Influence senior stakeholders and hold cross-functional teams accountable for delivering commercial priorities.</li> </ul> <h3>What We Are Looking For</h3> <ul> <li>Significant experience in ecommerce, digital trading or online retail, ideally within a fast-paced DTC or consumer business.</li> <li>Proven track record of owning website performance and delivering profitable commercial growth.</li> <li>Strong understanding of ecommerce trading metrics, including revenue, conversion, AOV, margin and customer lifetime value.</li> <li>Experience developing and executing trading strategies and onsite optimisation plans.</li> <li>Strong commercial judgement, with the ability to balance growth, profitability and customer experience.</li> <li>Highly analytical and data-driven, able to turn insight into clear commercial actions.</li> <li>Proactive and autonomous, with a strong bias for action and personal accountability.</li> <li>Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and lead cross-functional teams.</li> <li>Experience in testing, optimisation and continuous improvement.</li> <li>Confident using BI and ecommerce analytics tools, with an interest in leveraging AI and automation to improve performance.</li> <li>Clear communicator, comfortable challenging thinking and driving decisions at pace.</li> </ul> <h2>What’s in It for Me?</h2> <h3>Career Development</h3> <ul> <li> <p>Access bespoke development programmes designed by our in-house Learning & Development team.</p> </li> <li> <p>Develop your expertise through our upskilling programme, delivered in partnership with an industry-leading training provider.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Enhanced Leave</h3> <ul> <li> <p>25 days’ annual leave plus bank holidays.</p> </li> <li> <p>Enjoy your birthday off, on us!</p> </li> <li> <p>Enhanced maternity and paternity pay, depending on length of service.</p> </li> <li> <p>Up to 10 days’ compassionate leave.</p> </li> <li> <p>Option to buy up to 3 additional days of annual leave each year.</p> </li> <li> <p>Unlock 2 days of volunteer leave after 12 months.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Wellbeing Support</h3> <ul> <li> <p>Access face-to-face and virtual appointments with our in-house GP.</p> </li> <li> <p>Access our 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme, provided by Bupa.</p> </li> <li> <p>State-of-the-art on-site gym.</p> </li> <li> <p>Access to our on-site physiotherapist.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Other Perks</h3> <ul> <li> <p>Save up to 12% on personal tech through our salary sacrifice scheme.</p> </li> <li> <p>Subsidised bus pass from Manchester City Centre to our ICON office.</p> </li> <li> <p>Up to 50% staff discount on THG brands.</p> </li> <li> <p>On-site staff shop and barber.</p> </li> <li> <p>Refer someone to THG and receive up to £1,000 when they pass their probation.</p> </li> <li> <p>Anniversary gifts when you reach 5 and 10 years of service.</p> </li> </ul> <p>We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>THG is proud to be a Disability Confident Committed employer. If you are invited to interview, please let us know if there are any reasonable adjustments we can make to the recruitment process that will enable you to perform to the best of your ability.</strong></p> <p><strong>THG is committed to creating a diverse & inclusive environment and hence welcomes applications from all sections of the community.</strong></p> <p><strong>Because of the high volumes of applications our opportunities attract, it sometimes takes us time to review and consider them all. We endeavour to respond to every application we receive within 14 days. If you haven't heard from us within that time frame or should you have any specific questions about this or other applications for positions at THG please contact one of our <span class="mark75xs2u5gf" data-markjs="true" data-ogac="" data-ogab="" data-ogsc="" data-ogsb="">Talent</span> team to discuss further.</strong></p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

We move fast, challenge convention, and back ourselves to win. These values shape how we work every day.</p> <p data-start="580" data-end="776"><strong>About the role:</strong></p> <p data-start="580" data-end="776"></p> <p>We are looking to hire a Senior Events Manager to join our Brand Marketing team at Myprotein, the world’s largest online sports nutrition brand. In this senior role, you’ll take ownership of our end-to-end events strategy – leading a dynamic events calendar from concept through delivery, managing and developing a team of event professionals, and setting the standard for high-impact, brand-defining activations. With a strong focus on B2B and influencer-led events, you’ll build and maintain relationships with senior industry partners, stakeholders, and clients, shaping how the brand shows up at every touchpoint. You’ll partner closely with senior leadership, internal teams, and external partners to translate business objectives into bold event concepts delivered at scale.</p> <p><strong>What You'll Be Doing</strong></p> <ul> <li>Events and Activations strategy & calendar ownership</li> <li>Team leadership, coaching & development</li> <li>Budget ownership per activation</li> <li>Senior stakeholder & leadership engagement</li> <li>Supplier & vendor negotiation at scale</li> <li>B2B & flagship event execution</li> <li>On-site event leadership</li> <li>Speaker, talent & influencer partnerships (in collaboration with the influencer team)</li> <li>Brand direction for event materials & creative</li> <li>Multi-market event roll-out</li> <li>Logistics, scheduling & risk management</li> <li>Permits, compliance & health and safety</li> <li>Post-event reporting, ROI analysis & insight sharing</li> </ul> <p><strong>What We Look For your Skills, Knowledge and Experience:</strong></p> <p>We’re looking for a Senior Events Manager who leads from the front – someone who thrives under pressure, is energised by a fast-paced environment, and brings both strategic thinking and hands-on delivery to everything they do. You’ll have a sharp eye for industry trends, a track record of developing others, and the confidence to represent the brand in front of senior stakeholders.</p> <ul> <li>Experience: 5 years of event management experience, including experience operating at a senior or leadership level, ideally within a brand marketing, retail, or corporate environment.</li> <li>Brand Events: Proven track record delivering large-scale, influencer-focused and PR-driven events (e.g. global brand launches, PR previews, creator activations) end-to-end.</li> <li>Project Management: Proven ability to manage multiple complex, high-profile events simultaneously, from concept to execution.</li> <li>Stakeholder Management: Confident operating with senior stakeholders, internal teams, external partners, and vendors, including at exec level.</li> <li>Budgeting & Negotiation: Extensive experience owning event budgets, negotiating high-value contracts, and securing cost-effective, high-quality solutions.  </li> <li>Team Leadership: Proven experience leading, developing, and mentoring an events team, delegating effectively and overseeing event staff or external agencies.</li> <li>Strategic Planning: title: AI Engineer
description: <h2>Opportunity</h2> <p>Brunswick is on an exciting journey to harness the power of artificial intelligence and data science to enhance the way we work and the advice we provide to clients. As we continue to expand our AI capabilities, we are looking for an AI Engineer to join our growing team.</p> <p>In this role, you will be responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining AI-powered applications that deliver real value across the business. Working closely with our existing AI team, you will help build innovative solutions using modern AI technologies, with a particular focus on large language models (LLMs).</p> <p>This is an excellent opportunity for someone with hands-on experience developing and deploying AI applications who enjoys solving complex problems, working with a high degree of autonomy, and turning emerging technologies into practical, high-quality products.</p> <p>You will thrive in this role if you are curious, creative, and passionate about applying AI to solve real-world business challenges. They will have a strong academic background complemented by an outstanding career to date. Standout candidates will demonstrate:</p> <ul> <li>Experience building solutions with large language models (LLMs) and a deep understanding of the broader generative AI landscape.</li> <li>Experience designing datasets, conducting model evaluations, and fine-tuning foundation models to improve task-specific performance.</li> <li>Strong Python development skills, including experience writing production-quality code.</li> <li>Experience with front-end technologies such as JavaScript, React, HTML, and CSS.</li> <li>A solid understanding of statistics and machine learning fundamentals.</li> <li>An undergraduate degree in a quantitative discipline, such as Mathematics or Computer Science, or equivalent relevant industry experience.</li> <li>Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate technical concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.</li> <li>The ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment with changing priorities and an iterative, user-focused approach to development.</li> <li>Curiosity, a strong sense of ownership, and the ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively.</li> <li>Previous experience in professional services would be advantageous.</li> <li>Experience developing cloud applications on Microsoft Azure would be advantageous.</li> <li>Experience with DevOps practices and tools (e.g. CI/CD, Git) would be desirable.</li> <li>Knowledge of, or experience with, secure software development practices would be advantageous.</li> </ul> <h2>Why Join Us</h2> <p>Whether you are joining a client facing team, a core services team, or starting out on your professional career journey, joining Brunswick unlocks a range of employee benefits to support your financial future, health and wellness, family and community and continuous professional development.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h1>About Brunswick</h1> <p>Brunswick is a global advisory firm. They rely on us for deep experience, fresh perspectives and original thinking. So, in Brunswick you will find an exceptional range of experience and talent with a rich mix of backgrounds. From the beginning, we have prioritized attracting, developing, and retaining the best professionals in the industry, united by a culture of inclusivity, excellence, and intellectual curiosity.</p> <p>Founded in 1987 in London, the firm has organically grown to 27 offices in 18 countries across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia and Australia. It forecasts prices and volumes, holds a live view of our portfolio, and sets the fees on every quote. You'll join the pricing ML team and own key components of our dynamic pricing system. The direction is set. Within your components, choosing the bets and proving whether they worked is yours. This is a hands-on role. Most of your week will be writing and shipping production code, and you'll stay accountable for what that code does once it's live. You will: Own key components of our dynamic pricing system end to end, from design through to running them in production. Choose the bets within those components most likely to reduce sales adjustment, and show whether they worked. Make your components observable, guarded and replayable, so a wrong price is caught before a customer sees it. Unblock your own delivery across engineering, platform and commercial teams. Within your components, choose between competing bets based on which is most likely to move the metric, and stop the ones that don't. Design experiments and holdouts that work with low-volume, high-value deals, where a textbook A/B test often isn't possible. Run it live, safely Build the monitoring, alerting, guardrails and staged release your components need. That includes detecting drift, catching runaway feedback loops and holding unexpected price moves for review. Make any pricing decision your components produce reproducible after the fact, for debugging and for regulators. Work with the Price Quoting squad and ML Platform so models are built for production from the start, not handed over at the end. Close the loop with the business Find out why sales teams adjust prices, and turn those reasons into model inputs or new bets. Explain model behaviour and trade-offs to engineers, product and commercial colleagues clearly enough that they can act on it. Redesign the team's recurring pricing workflows with AI built in, such as feedback triage, daily price review and experiment write-ups. Decide which steps stay human. 🎯 🎯 Requirements: Must-haves: You build. Most of your current role is writing and shipping production code, and you want to keep it that way. This is not a people leadership role or an architecture role where others implement. You have owned a live ML system that made automated decisions with money attached, for example in algorithmic trading, dynamic pricing, marketplaces, ad bidding, credit or betting. You have dealt with its failures in production, such as feedback loops, silent drift, bad outputs reaching customers and rollbacks, and changed how you build because of them. Strong probabilistic modelling and decision-making under uncertainty, such as pricing, conversion or elasticity modelling, and experimentation. You formulate the problem from first principles and pick the simplest approach that works. You've run ML as production services on modern cloud infrastructure: containerised models behind APIs, event-driven microservices, infrastructure as code and CI/CD on AWS or similar. Your model changes go through the same pipeline, tests and rollback as any other code, so shipping one on a Thursday afternoon is routine. Production-grade Python, and a habit of designing for observability, testing and replay. You work as a peer with software engineers. A track record of moving a commercial metric, working alongside product managers and commercial stakeholders to get there. You use AI tooling as a day-to-day multiplier on your own work, and you know where it fails. Energy experience is not required. We will teach you the market. What we can't teach quickly is the judgement that comes from running a live pricing or trading system. Bonus points: Experience in energy, commodities or other markets where prices, forecasts and risk interact. Contextual bandits, causal inference or Bayesian methods used in production. Stochastic optimisation or operations research. A PhD in a field such as maths, physics, computer science or operations research. ✨ Benefits & Perks: Salary: Competitive. We are looking to pay £115,000 or equivalent in local currency. Stock Options: everyone on the team has ownership in our mission. 25 days holiday + public holidays. Up to £150 / €150 monthly on anything that supports your wellbeing, from therapy to gym memberships to meditation apps. 🗣️ Interview Process: Our processes normally take around 2-3 weeks from first call to offer. Please let us know about any adjustments to timelines that may be required. First call with our Talent Team (30 mins). This is to understand your experience, motivations, and discuss the role in more detail. Behavioural interview with our Rosso GM, hiring manager for this role (30 mins). A bit about us: 🚀 We’re building at the forefront of AI technology, without losing the deeply human expertise our clients depend on. 🏢 Orbital is built with former practising real estate lawyers and 250+ years of combined legal expertise. We're purpose-built for the complexity of real estate: accelerating due diligence, drafting and negotiation, and deal coordination with legal-grade precision. 💰 We've just raised a $60m Series B, led by Brighton Park Capital, to accelerate our global expansion – $75m raised to date. 🤝 We're trusted by 5,000+ real estate professionals, spanning UK Magic Circle and US Am Law 100 firms, to household names like M&S. Leading firms like BCLP, Orrick, Goodwin, Womble Bond Dickinson and Clifford Chance rely on Orbital to remove the busywork, freeing legal and real estate teams to focus on sharp judgment, standout client service, and closing deals faster. 💡 Working at Orbital means joining a bold, ambitious team, with the trust to take ownership and make a real impact from day one. The Role Orbital has been scaling fast, and we’re scaling or security and compliance with it. We're hiring a senior, London-based InfoSec Lead to own our information security due diligence, compliance, and vendor risk end-to-end - bringing structure and consistency to work that's currently covered on a contractor basis. Whilst experience in IT operations or IT management is helpful, the Infosec Lead and IT Manager report independently to our Head of Operations and own separate (but naturally interconnected) remits. You’ll also work closely with Engineering, Product, Legal and our external Infosec support, to keep security and compliance embedded in how the business runs, not bolted on after the fact. What You'll Own InfoSec & Compliance Delivery You will: Own our InfoSec strategy and roadmap : set the direction for how security and compliance scale with the business, not just an executor; identify control gaps and weaknesses, prioritize remediation, and track it through to completion. Own our risk program : run risk identification, assessment and treatment, keep the risk register current. You're making the call on what's an acceptable risk. Own third party risk assurance, in both directions : run vendor security reviews for vendors we bring on (or are renewing with) and own customer & vendor due diligence (DDQs) when we’re the ones being assessed. Pull in support required from the rest of the business and jump on client calls when needed to resolve DDQs. Drive automation on the DDQ side specifically, so it doesn’t eat a disproportionate share of your time as the function matures. Own our existing and future compliance certifications: you’ll be responsible for maintaining compliance with existing standards (ISO 27001 and SOC2 Type 2) and pursuing future certifications relevant to us. Management of the compliance program will be end-to-end, and involve ISMS management reviews, quarterly access control reviews, audit evidence gathering, scheduling and remediation tracking. This also includes keeping policy & public-facing security documentation (eg. our trust centre) current - so certification is a continuously-run capability rather than a periodic scramble. Partner cross-functionally : work with Engineering, Product, and Legal to embed security and compliance requirements into how we build and sell, and stay close enough to product changes that customer-facing security information is always accurate. What We're Looking For Significant senior in-house or scale-up InfoSec leadership experience : you've owned due diligence, vendor review, and compliance work end-to-end inside a fast-moving business, not just advised from the outside. Strong understanding of cloud & cloud security, and ideally previous technical background in IT Security or SWE / DevOps. A track record of scaling due-diligence processes , not just running them manually, you know how to spot what can be templated, automated, or self-served, and you make that happen rather than just wishing for it. Comfortable being close to engineering : you don't need to write code, but you're happy sitting in technical conversations, understanding product changes, and knowing enough about IT systems to weigh in sensibly on security-sensitive changes. Pragmatic and delivery-focused : you know the difference between a genuine risk and a distraction, and you keep due diligence and audit work moving at commercial pace rather than becoming a bottleneck. AI-literacy with working familiarity with AI governance (ISO 42001, EU AI Act etc). Comfortable operating independently : this is an individual-contributor role to start, with real ownership of the roadmap rather than a narrow, audit-only remit. Working knowledge of privacy law is important (GDPR/CCPA/US state privacy laws) to partner with our legal function. Why This Might Not Be For You You want to run day-to-day IT operations or manage IT staff. That sits with our IT Manager, not this role. You prefer tasks defined and handed to you. This is a role for an independent decision maker... you're expected to identify what needs doing, set the plan, and drive it to closure yourself, not wait to be briefed. You feel more comfortable with a narrowly-defined, audit-only remit. This role sits close to Engineering, Product, and Legal, and is expected to actively reduce manual DDQ overhead over time, not just process tickets. Why Join Orbital Shape how security and compliance scale with the business... the processes and playbooks here are still being built. Genuine cross-functional influence: you'll be close to Engineering, Product, and Legal, not sitting outside them. Genuine momentum: $60m Series B, doubling headcount, expanding across two continents. Work alongside a leadership team that treats security as a business enabler, not just a risk function. 🔒 Security is everyone’s responsibility at Orbital. We ask all team members to follow our security policies, complete regular awareness training, and handle sensitive data with care in line with ISO 27001 standards. Spot something unusual? Reporting risks or incidents quickly helps us maintain the strong culture of security and compliance we all depend on. 💡 At Orbital, we’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We especially welcome applications from people who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. title: Senior Implementation Engineer
description: We’re Heidi. We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. In just 18 months, our clinical AI products have absorbed the administrative chaos of 73 million patient visits. Today, we support over 2.5 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries. Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s healthcare capacity and strengthen the human connection at its heart. We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again. If you don’t choose easy and you want to build something way bigger than yourself, then choose the challenge, choose Heidi. The role The Software Implementation Engineer is a hands-on technical delivery role at the centre of complex NHS deployments. At Heidi, the CSM owns the customer from day one: the relationship, the rollout plan, the path to renewal. The Implementation Engineer is the technical arm they lean on: the person who personally configures SSO with the customer's IT team, sets up and provisions tenants, delivers EHR integrations through to go-live, configures agents and custom builds, and gives every technical problem a fast diagnosis and the right owner — fixing what is configuration, and handing confirmed product defects to Support Engineering, who own and drive their resolution. You are the reason launches don't stall on technical topics. The remit is deliberately broad: anything to do with getting an account set up, configured and optimised is yours, from account configuration and MFA through to integration build and iteration, rather than being split across several specialist roles. Clinical training and adoption sit with Clinical Enablement, not here. Your ownership begins upon acceptance of the enterprise handover. It ends when the agreed technical scope has passed its acceptance criteria, customer sign-off has been recorded, the final configuration has been documented and the implementation has transferred into hypercare or BAU support. You are technically credible in front of a CIO, precise in what you hand to engineers, and relentless about closing the loop — and you translate what customers need technically into clear, prioritised asks for the Technical Program Manager (TPM), who owns the integration roadmap and prioritisation. Success in this role looks like: Hands-on delivery — you personally set up, configure and validate the technical footprint of an account: identity, provisioning, integrations, agents, data flows. Not coordinated — done. Technical ownership — every technical problem at your accounts gets a fast diagnosis and a clear owner. What is configuration or implementation, you fix; what is a product defect, Support Engineering owns and drives — you hand it over with the diagnosis attached and do not shadow the ticket. CSMs never have to diagnose or route technical problems themselves. Fast unblocking — technical blockers that would stall a launch for weeks get diagnosed, sequenced and resolved in days, because you understand the problem and know exactly who has to do what. Clean boundaries — you hand net-new build work to FDEs as precise, prioritised requirements they can act on without rework, and you route live product defects to Support Engineering with a proper diagnosis attached — you don’t hoard work that belongs elsewhere, and you don’t toss problems over walls. Trusted translation — customer IT and security teams treat you as a peer; the Technical Program Manager (TPM) gets integration gaps and technical priorities from you they can act on, and product hears a clear, prioritised signal. This is a delivery-accountable role, so your job is to make the technical side of every account work: identity live, tenants configured, integrations delivered, agents built, security questions answered, and technical problems solved before they become escalations. What you’ll do Technical Onboarding & Account Setup Own the technical setup of new enterprise accounts end to end: tenant and workspace configuration, user provisioning and seat structure, environment readiness. Configure SSO with the customer’s IT team — SAML / OIDC against Okta, Microsoft Entra and NHS identity infrastructure — including MFA and conditional-access alignment. Drive network and device readiness: whitelisting, VDI and shared-device constraints, mobile device management, so clinicians can actually use Heidi on day one. Work directly with customer IT to clear whatever is blocking a swift deployment: deployment questionnaires, IT vetting, access requests, environment prerequisites. Integration Delivery Receive the validated integration design and signed SOW from presales. Confirm implementation prerequisites, elaborate the agreed design where necessary, configure the Heidi components, perform technical testing, support customer UAT and execute the technical go-live activities within the implementation plan you own. Translate the agreed SOW and technical design into precise, prioritised implementation requirements; hand net-new build to FDEs in a form they can act on without rework, own the account-side delivery around it, and surface integration gaps to the Technical Program Manager. Raise any requirement that is missing, materially different or genuinely out of scope through formal change control before work proceeds, rather than absorbing scope creep silently. Provide credible estimates, identify dependencies early and give the CSM evidence-based status and recovery options. You own the integrated technical plan, customer-facing delivery dates and dependency escalation. After go-live, keep working with the trust integration team to iterate and optimise the integration: anything that is not a product defect is yours to make work. Product-technical Configuration Set up agentic workflows, agents and custom builds to fit each account’s clinical and operational workflows, turning vague customer asks into scoped configurations with clear acceptance criteria. Translate what the customer bought into what has to be configured, and set it up: products, identity, integrations, agents, APIs, exports and data flows. As Heidi adds products (agents, agentic workflows, comms), their account-level setup lands here too. Handle technical template and coding setup where it crosses into system behaviour (clinical content stays with Clinical Enablement). Technical Escalation & Resolution During active implementation and hypercare, be the first technical port of call for CSMs: when something technical breaks or will not configure, you provide first-line diagnosis and make sure it lands with the right owner. Once an account has formally handed over to BAU, Support Engineering owns initial triage and ongoing incident management, and you are re-engaged only through agreed escalation criteria. Diagnose before you route: implementation-phase and account-specific configuration issues are yours to fix; confirmed product defects go to Support Engineering with your diagnosis attached — they own and drive resolution, and Support Engineering owns defect resolution. The Implementation Engineer remains informed where the defect affects implementation milestones, acceptance criteria or customer readiness, without duplicating Support’s investigation. Translate customer technical problems into clear priorities — routing integration gaps to the Technical Program Manager (who owns the roadmap) and confirmed defects to Support Engineering — the alignment that gets problems actually solved. Information Governance & Security Enablement Provide accurate technical input and evidence for DPIAs, security questionnaires and IT-assurance requests, routed through Compliance, who owns these processes. Security, Privacy and Clinical Safety retain approval authority for their respective positions. Keep them off the critical path without becoming the sign-off owner. Work within NHS governance gates — clinical safety sign-off, IG approval, change-control windows — planning technical work around them (clinical-safety substance is owned by Heidi’s Clinical Safety Officer). Handover acceptance and scope control Review the signed SOW, discovery notes, technical decision record, architecture, acceptance criteria, success measures and open risk log before technical implementation begins. Return the handover where a blocking material risk, unclear scope or unsupported commitment prevents a credible implementation plan. Deliver against the agreed scope without converting new customer requirements into configuration work. Classify emerging requests as in-scope configuration, defect, net-new engineering, roadmap request or commercial change. Escalate material scope changes through the CSM, SE and AE before committing work or dates. How we show up Build for the next decade, not next quarter . Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism. Lead, don't wait . We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that. Follow the evidence . Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford. Own the outcome . Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander. Ship, measure, go again . A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless. Live in clinicians' reality . Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it. Why Heidi? You’ll join a team focused on real-world impact over imaginary valuations and glossy PR. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders, and designers who’ve felt the moral and practical toll of what non-care feels like. True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally. Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose to build something that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognise that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it. The work is hard, but you will trust and admire the people you work beside, and rest easy knowing you’re doing the defining work of your career. Our Benefits Equity from day one. When Heidi wins, you win. You'll share directly in the success you help create. Your health, covered. Comprehensive private medical and dental cover through Bupa, plus 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder and a £100/month Healthy Heidi’s stipend. Global parental leave . 26 weeks paid for primary carers and 18 weeks for secondary carers, subject to eligibility. Fertility support . £7,000 one-off payment, eligibility applies. Learning & development. £700 per year for courses, books, memberships, conferences and more. Home office budget of £500 one-off to set up a workspace you actually want to work in. Recharge days after major milestones and busy periods so you can reset and come back strong. Work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks per year, wherever the world takes y

title: AI Solutions Lead
description: Our Mission: Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement. Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them. Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here . The Role AI is changing what it means to deploy enterprise software. Configuring a customer's procurement workflows used to mean weeks of manual setup, integration by integration, edge case by edge case. Increasingly, that first-draft build work can be directed rather than done by hand: AI agents can generate workflow configurations, draft integration mappings, and produce the initial pass on a customer's setup. The job shifts with it. Instead of building every workflow yourself, you specify exactly what needs to exist, direct AI to build it, and apply the judgment AI can't: is this the right configuration for this customer's approval policy, will Legal and Finance actually sign off on it, does it hold up once real spend starts flowing through it. In practice, that might mean catching that the approval chain AI just drafted works perfectly for HQ, but misses a regional delegation-of-authority rule that would fail an audit in the customer's APAC entity. As Omnea's AI Solutions Lead, you own deployment of the Omnea platform end to end - typically running 3-5 enterprise deployments concurrently - for some of Europe's most recognisable companies. You advise customers on the best-fit configuration, direct AI-assisted build work to get there fast, and validate every output against what the customer actually needs. You'll also deal with the politics that come with every enterprise rollout: the Legal team wanting one more sign-off, the Finance stakeholder who doesn't trust the new approval flow, the exec sponsor who's gone quiet. You become the internal voice of the customer, and you're judged on outcomes you can point to: time to launch, post-go-live CSAT, and whether that customer becomes a case study or reference. This is an early hire on Omnea's customer team, working directly with our sales, customer, product, and engineering leadership. The future shape of the role is yours to define! What You'll Do Discover and design Run discovery with customer stakeholders across Procurement, Finance, Legal, and IT, and translate their process into an Omnea configuration Design the target workflow: approval chains, routing logic, integrations, and the edge cases that make procurement hard On a deployment with a dozen-plus integrations, you own the sequencing - what has to land first, what blocks what - and the harder calls underneath it: which system is the source of truth for a given entity, and how records reconcile when two systems key that entity differently Define success criteria and a realistic path to go-live with the customer's project sponsor Build with AI, not instead of it You're not just directing AI to draft your own deliverables faster - you're configuring the specialized agents Omnea's customers rely on every day: an intake agent that knows how to ask a procurement analyst the right follow-up question, a risk agent that flags what actually matters to this customer's Legal team The real leverage comes from chaining agents together - an intake agent that hands clean, structured requests to a risk agent, which in turn routes into approvals with the right context already attached. You design how those agents work as a system, not just individually Writing a spec for one agent is a skill. Writing one that holds up across a chain of agents - where one agent's output becomes another's input - is the actual bar here Validate every AI-generated output against the customer's actual process, policy, and edge cases before anything ships Handle what AI can't: judgment calls on ambiguous requirements, custom logic, and anything that needs a human read on internal politics Deploy and prove value Present configured workflows to stakeholders, from procurement analysts to CFOs, working through the pushback and internal politics that come with any enterprise rollout, and win their buy-in Run multi-day onsite workshops with customers, coordinating dozens of stakeholders across multiple workstreams at once - a different muscle than a single stakeholder meeting Project-manage the deployment: timelines, blockers, stakeholder alignment, and a clear path to launch, acting as an extension of the customer's team Track adoption after go-live and keep the configuration working as the customer's process evolves Work with Product and Engineering during the design phase, not just after something breaks in the field - you're often the earliest signal on whether a new module will hold up for an enterprise customer, and that shapes what gets built next What's Different About This Role You'll spend more time specifying and validating than building from scratch. AI produces the first draft; you make sure it's right for this customer Writing instructions AI can act on precisely is a skill you'll build fast here. Vague requests produce vague configurations Judgment matters more, not less. AI speeds up the build, but you decide whether the output is right for this contract, this Board, this customer You'll keep experimenting as our AI tooling evolves, and share what works with the rest of the team About You We don't expect you to know how to do all of this on day one. TL;DR: you're ambitious and hard-working, as comfortable directing an AI agent through a tricky configuration as you are presenting a project plan to an exec. You make up for any gap in experience with hunger and a genuine growth mindset. You derive energy from building relationships, shipping projects, and making customers succeed. 4-8 years in a fast-paced, high-bar environment: a startup, scale-up, consulting, banking, or something you built yourself Less experience? Check out our Solutions Associate role Comfortable directing AI tools to produce first-draft work, and confident enough in your own judgment to catch what's wrong. Prior use of tools like ChatGPT, Claude, or Cursor is a strong plus. What matters most is your ability to write clear, specific instructions and evaluate what comes back Client-facing experience, or the natural gravitas to be excellent at it. You can point to a time you went well beyond what a client expected A track record of doing something exceptionally well, whether that's work, academia, sport, or anything else you've put your mind to Comfortable reasoning about system architecture - how data models, primary keys, and integration sequencing interact across a dozen enterprise systems. You don't need to write the integration code, but you need to know why it breaks and be able to reason with the people who do, and you'll need to become an Omnea product expert You build real relationships with people at any level, from a junior procurement analyst to a CFO, and know how to handle pushback and stakeholder politics, not just build rapport Comfortable running rooms of stakeholders across a genuinely cross-functional tool - on a single project you'll interface with the CPO, Legal, Finance, AP, InfoSec, and Compliance, plus each of their technical resources, often all with competing priorities on the same decision Comfortable moving between the detail and the big picture: configuring a workflow in the morning, presenting a project plan to an exec in the afternoon Entrepreneurial, have high ownership, and want to be part of building something. title: Principal Database Engineer
description: Building the Future of Open Finance Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. The team Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. Kraken’s Core Infrastructure Engineering team builds and operates the shared data systems behind critical production services. Our estate spans on-premises and cloud infrastructure, with MariaDB at its centre and Kafka, Redis and Elasticsearch across the wider platform. We’re hiring a Principal Database Engineer to bring long-term experience and technical judgment to this estate. You’ll assess it, set the goals and direction, and work hands-on with the team to deliver measurable improvements. This is an individual contributor role with influence across teams and several quarters of work. The opportunity Review the estate against business needs and production evidence. Judge reliability, scale, cost and operational complexity, identifying what should be preserved and where investment or simplification would make a difference. Define the target architecture and measurable goals. Agree a prioritised roadmap with engineering leads and dependent teams, explaining the trade-offs and sequencing work around delivery risks. Execute that roadmap with the team through design, implementation and adoption. Stay personally involved in difficult migrations and scaling decisions, with representative benchmarks, data-integrity checks and credible cutover and rollback plans. Adapt the plan as evidence changes and verify the results in production before calling the work complete. Investigate difficult MariaDB failures and performance limits through the engine, storage and application behaviour. Improve fleet reliability through useful observability, safer changes and tested backup, restore and disaster recovery procedures. Set recovery objectives with service owners and prove them through exercises. Build and maintain production software for database provisioning, upgrades and routine maintenance. Make self-service workflows safe and auditable, incorporating access controls and change evidence with Security and Compliance. Work with application teams on schemas, transaction boundaries, queries and data-store choices. Make the operational consequences clear and resolve dependencies that span teams. Mentor engineers across the team through design reviews, pairing and incident analysis. Help them deepen their database expertise and take ownership of technical decisions. Participate in on-call and incident response, leaving clear operational ownership and following through on lessons from production. What you bring 8+ years operating and evolving production database estates at scale. You have assessed inherited systems, set technical direction and delivered improvements with engineering teams, and can explain how those decisions held up over time. Strong understanding of high availability, replication and distributed database failure modes. You can explain consistency and availability trade-offs and reason about transaction boundaries and reliable event delivery, including transactional outbox patterns. Deep, recent hands-on MariaDB expertise, including InnoDB, MVCC and transaction isolation, locking, query optimisation, binary logs and MariaDB GTID replication. You can explain the mechanisms and diagnostic evidence behind your decisions. Personal ownership of MariaDB incident diagnosis, performance tuning and tested restore or point-in-time recovery. You can explain what you did, how you established data integrity and what remained uncertain. Strong software engineering skills in Python, Go, Rust or a comparable language. You have personally built and maintained production software or automation for database workflows such as provisioning, failover, online schema changes and self-service operations, using version control, code review and delivery pipelines, with tested failure handling. Strong low-level Linux, Kernel, storage and networking fundamentals, with the ability to investigate problems beyond the database process. Clear written technical judgment and demonstrated delivery across teams without reporting-line authority. You help stakeholders make sound database design and lifecycle decisions, and develop experienced engineers through shared delivery. Nice to haves Experience operating databases in containerised, hybrid on-premises/cloud or multi-region environments. Familiarity with Kubernetes, infrastructure as code or GitOps, including their operational trade-offs. Experience with database proxies or load-balancing layers (MaxScale, HAProxy, ProxySQL, or similar). Experience with PostgreSQL, Vitess, TiDB, ScyllaDB, ClickHouse or internal database platforms; operational knowledge of Kafka, Redis/Valkey or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch. Experience in regulated environments or contributions to database engines, operators and other infrastructure software. title: FIX Onboarding & Client Services
description: FIX Onboarding & Client Services, EMEA Hybrid, London, UK (3+ days per week in-office) | Full-Time About Us Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year ( Risk.net ). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 60+ of the world's leading liquidity providers. We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems. The Role We are seeking a motivated and technically curious Onboarding and Client Services professional to join our London team. This role will focus on FIX client onboarding, integrations, and client service delivery across FX, equities and digital assets. The successful candidate will work closely with clients and internal teams to ensure seamless connectivity, smooth integration, and exceptional service throughout the client lifecycle. We're building genuinely AI-enabled tooling to support this function — so this role is less about arriving with a decade of FIX expertise already committed to memory, and much more about someone sharp, adaptable, and genuinely curious who can use that tooling to go further, faster, and think proactively about how the process itself should keep improving. What You'll Work On FIX Onboarding & Integrations: Lead and manage FIX client onboarding projects — from initial requirements gathering through certification and production go-live. Configure, test, and validate FIX sessions, including order routing, execution reporting, and market data flows. Coordinate conformance testing and certification with clients to ensure compliance with platform standards. Document onboarding procedures, client configurations, and integration best practices. Leverage internal AI and automation tools to streamline client onboarding and troubleshooting — including tooling built specifically for this function, giving you a genuine head start on deep process knowledge. Collaborate with engineering and product teams to support new FIX workflows, APIs, and client integration initiatives. Client Services: Serve as frontline technical support for clients in EMEA across FX and equities business lines. Build and maintain strong client relationships, ensuring timely and transparent communication addressing their needs and queries with professionalism and efficiency. Provide ongoing technical and operational support for production trading environments. Manage client inquiries, troubleshoot workflow or configuration issues, and coordinate resolutions across internal teams. Partner with account management, sales and product teams to ensure a positive client experience and successful delivery of platform enhancements. What We Need 2-5 years of experience in a client onboarding, integration, or technical support role within financial technology, trading, or brokerage. Good working knowledge of the FIX protocol — message structures, session management, and common trading workflows. Genuine comfort troubleshooting FIX connectivity, analysing logs, and resolving integration issues, with the judgement to know when to dig deeper. Familiarity with FX and Equities trading environments, order lifecycle management, and market data connectivity — genuine interest in working across multiple asset classes rather than staying within one. A genuinely proactive, tech-first mindset — someone who treats our AI and automation tooling as a way to go further and faster, not a replacement for good judgement, and who naturally looks for ways to improve a process rather than simply following it. Excellent communication and organisational skills, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple onboarding/client projects in parallel. Nice-to-have: Experience with OMS/EMS platforms, liquidity aggregators, or trading system integrations. Exposure to other API protocols and architectures (REST, WebSocket) — relevant given the depth of our own API. Scripting or automation experience (e.g. Python) and familiarity with monitoring tools (Splunk, Grafana, or similar). Understanding of financial market structure and post-trade workflows. What You Get A genuinely rich API to work with — not a thin FIX wrapper bolted onto a legacy system. You'll onboard clients onto an API with real depth across order routing, execution reporting, and market data — the kind of platform where understanding the protocol properly actually matters. Breadth across FX, Equities, and digital assets — most FIX/onboarding roles sit inside a single asset class. Here you'll build knowledge across all three, at a network connecting 40+ liquidity providers — exposure that compounds faster than a single-product environment. Real ownership of the tech-to-business bridge — you're not just configuring sessions, you're the person translating FIX/API detail into client outcomes clients actually care about. That combination — technical credibility plus commercial judgement, is the actual shape of this role. A genuinely tech-first operation — we've built dedicated AI tooling for this function specifically, so your ramp-up is faster and your day-to-day is spent on the client and integration problems that need real judgement, not repetitive configuration work. title: Sr. Compliance Consultant
description: About Us Condukt is the next-generation compliance platform for financial services, offering an agentic solution powered by real-time data for business identity. Always-on and policy-aware, Condukt enables financial institutions and fintechs to gain actionable insights into business verification - unlocking growth, increasing efficiency, and strengthening compliance. We were founded by former operators and builders with deep experience in banking, payments, and lending. Today, our team spans across London and Porto, bringing together engineers, product owners, and operators from companies like Revolut, Meta, Block (Square), SumUp, American Express, Yandex, and OakNorth. Trusted by leading regulated entities, including Wise, Tide, Mollie, Shift4, Flatpay, and myPOS, Condukt is backed by top investors, including Lightspeed Venture Partners and MMC Ventures. Position Overview We’re looking for a Senior Compliance Consultant to help our clients navigate regulatory change, horizon-scan upcoming regulation, and overcome regulatory challenges so they can transform their businesses and meet their strategic growth objectives. This is a versatile, high-impact role at the intersection of regulation, client advisory, practical delivery and product strategy. Your mission is to deeply understand our clients’ needs and regulatory obligations, and to deliver solutions that help them achieve their compliance and business outcomes. You’ll stay ahead of the risk and compliance landscape, translating regulatory change into clear guidance for our customers and concrete requirements for our Product team. Whether you’re shaping a client’s regulatory strategy or influencing our product roadmap, you’ll bring deep knowledge and hands-on experience of financial crime compliance, along with strong commercial awareness. Acting as an in-house consultant, you’ll connect long-term regulatory horizons with granular operational realities. As an early-stage, fast-growing company, we value people who take ownership, move comfortably between complex challenges, and have the judgement to turn them into sharp, practical solutions. You’ll also work on long-horizon strategic projects, such as building government relationships and expanding Condukt’s global data footprint, where progress is measured in weeks, not months. If you thrive in dynamic environments where no two days look the same, enjoy tackling a constant stream of new and complex problems, and want to help shape how financial institutions and fintechs approach compliance, this role is for you. What you’ll do: Act as Condukt’s subject matter expert on KYB/KYC and AML/CFT, giving clients clear, commercially minded advice on their regulatory obligations Lead client engagements end to end, from understanding the business challenge and assessing current controls to designing solutions that combine Condukt’s platform with third-party providers and supporting their implementation Produce high-quality, client-ready deliverables, such as gap analyses, risk assessments, onboarding and monitoring frameworks, policies and decision papers Run workshops with client stakeholders, from compliance teams to the C-suite, turning discussion into practical next steps Horizon-scan regulation across the UK, Europe and beyond, and brief clients on what’s coming and what it means for them, directly or alongside our commercial team Advise clients on their compliance stack, testing and benchmarking providers through structured, RFP-style evaluations Build and maintain relationships with regulators, government bodies and company registers to secure access to data, expand Condukt’s global footprint and represent Condukt in industry forums Shape Condukt’s advisory proposition, identifying emerging client needs and opportunities to bring new capabilities to existing clients alongside our commercial team Partner with Product to translate regulatory and client needs into the signals, data and capabilities we build Contribute to business development and thought leadership with a clear, well-argued point of view on regulation, through proposals, client pitches, whitepapers, briefings, webinars and industry events What you bring: 4+ years’ experience in financial crime compliance, gained in a consultancy, a regulator or a regulated financial services firm Deep domain expertise in risk and compliance, ideally across KYB/KYC, AML/CFT or business onboarding in financial services A track record of advising financial institutions and fintechs on risk, compliance or regulatory matters, with a toolkit of structured frameworks you can adapt to a fast-growing company Experience leading client engagements and producing polished, client-ready deliverables Experience You'll be the customer's technical advocate inside CoreWeave from contract through delivery, onboarding and day-to-day operations, and you'll drive the programs that get their capacity into production.</p> <p>We're hiring at Senior and Staff levels. Staff TSMs take our largest, multi-site accounts and lead programs across the team.</p> <p><strong>In this role, you will:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own the technical relationship with your customers' engineering and executive leaders, and be the person they trust to tell them what's really happening.</li> <li>Run delivery and onboarding programs end to end, from contract and site readiness to the day the customer runs production work on new capacity.</li> <li>Read each account's health every week, catch problems early, and drive cross-team issues to an owner and a resolution.</li> <li>Coordinate Fleet Operations, Capacity, data center, support and engineering teams on your customers' behalf, leading through influence.</li> <li>Carry customer needs into Product and Engineering and follow them through to a decision, then close the loop with the customer.</li> <li>Partner with account executives on one customer message, and with Specialist Field Engineers on technical depth.</li> <li>Help the team scale: improve our playbooks and tooling, interview, and mentor newer TSMs.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Who You Are</strong></h2> <ul> <li>5+ years in technical program management, technical account management, solutions architecture, customer success engineering or professional services delivery with cloud infrastructure customers. Employment offers are conditional upon receiving satisfactory check results.</em></p> <p><strong>What We Offer</strong></p> <p>In addition to a competitive salary, we offer a variety of benefits to support your needs, including:</p> <ul> <li>Family-level Medical Insurance</li> <li>Family-level Dental Insurance </li> <li>Generous Pension Contribution </li> <li>Life Assurance at 4x Salary </li> <li>Critical Illness Cover </li> <li>Employee Assistance Programme </li> <li>Tuition Reimbursement</li> <li>Work culture focused on innovative disruption</li> </ul> <p><em>Benefits may vary by location. </em></p> <p><strong>Equal Opportunity </strong></p> <p><em>CoreWeave is an equal opportunity employer, committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive workplace. Under the GDPR and the UK GDPR, you have the right to request access to your personal data, to request that your personal data be rectified or erased, and to request that processing of your personal data be restricted.
